section.paragraph: Working notes (hidden; not part of the submitted calculation): how this edition was produced, its tool status and the open bookkeeping items.

Distilled from the pile design notebook (package 8db9964e721f), case "End Bent 2 piles: 18 in square prestressed concrete, FBMP fixed run". Same inputs, equations and load combinations as the notebook; results should match its exported report. Blockpad edition written by pile_design/bpad.py (scripts/build_pile_bpad.py) from the same case; every definition was evaluated independently and compared with the notebook to 1 part in 10⁹.
Status: All numerical checks pass (largest ratio 1.00) · 15 pending item(s) remain.

• FBMP source: End Bent 2_Fixed.XML, SHA-256 3543df298b92593ce9bac14f9228ffacf5b0ce7e76b5e1d887ae228ef811a90e (registered export EB2-XML). 4 piles at 4.5 ft; cutoff elevation 41.2567 ft, ground 23.59 ft.

• Every definition was read back from the XML and evaluated by an independent Blockpad-syntax evaluator, then compared with the notebook (and with the Mathcad worksheet) before the file was written. Governing records, the notebook angles, the neutral-axis depth c_gov and the few values found by a search over the interaction sweep are amber inputs read from the notebook.

The notebook lists 15 PENDING items; the distilled ratios above do not close them: Axial compression · maximum Pu / φPn,max; Axial + biaxial flexure · LRFD Eq. 5.6.4.5-3; Axial + flexure · resultant bending axis (strain compatibility); Shear · general procedure; Service I concrete tension; Minimum square pile size (Table 3.5.1-1); Pile-to-cap moment transfer (embedment below 48 in); Pile Data Table completeness (SDM 11.4); Environment classification; Pile-to-cap connection (12 in embedment); Downdrag source documented; FBMP export current; Minimum tip elevation; Scour resistance and elevations; Drivability.
The Status covers the recomputed numerical checks only; it is not design acceptance.
Inputs pending confirmation (captions carried "[pending confirmation]" in the notebook): DD_tons, R_scour_net_tons, R_scour_total_tons, soil_type, S_u, environment, f_y_spiral.
A ✓ status covers only the recomputed numerical checks; it is not design acceptance. The pending items of the notebook stay open. Recalculate in Blockpad after any input change.

report.paragraph: Codes: AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, 10th edition (2024): 5.6.4.4, 5.6.4.5, 5.6.6.1, 5.7.3.3, 5.7.3.4.2, 5.9.2.3.2, 5.12.9.4; FDOT Structures Design Guidelines (SDG) 3.5 and Structures Detailing Manual (SDM) 11.4, January 2026; Standard Plans Index 455.
Inputs are highlighted amber; results are the green tables.
• FBMP analysis: End Bent 2_Fixed.XML. 4 piles at 4.5 ft; cutoff elevation 41.2567 ft, ground 23.59 ft.
• Pile: Standard Plans Index 455-018 (18 in square), strand pattern 12~0.6, spiral 0.034 in² wire at 6 in.

• Downdrag 18 tons per pile is a drag load DR: gamma_DR = 1.1 (strength) and 1 (Service I) in the structural demands (LRFD Table 3.4.1-1, 10.7.3.7); it is excluded from the Factored Design Load and added nominally to the required bearing resistance (SDG Eq. 3-1, phi = 0.75).
• The interaction curve of Figure 2 is a picture of the interaction sweep. The 5.6.4.5 route, the resultant-axis check at c_gov, the demands and every ratio are live formulas.

axial compression D/C, largest Pu / phi Pn,max

• Strain is linear with the extreme compression fiber at eps_cu = 0.003 and a neutral-axis depth c swept geometrically from 4H to 0.02H in the interaction sweep (H = depth of the section normal to the bending axis). Strand strain = eps_pe + eps_ce + eps_cu (d - c)/c.

• Strand stress: PCI power formula for Grade 270 low-relaxation strand in tension, Ep eps in compression (no correction for displaced concrete). Concrete: rectangular block a = beta1 c on the compressed part of the square (chamfers ignored).
• Pn is held between -Aps fpy and Pn,max; phi runs from 0.75 to 1.00 as the net tensile strain goes from 0.002 to 0.005. The pure-compression and pure-tension points are scalars below.

• The 121-point sweep is not written as formulas. Figure 2 is a picture of the interaction sweep. Section 9 evaluates the same equations (strain, power-formula stress, block geometry, Pn, Mn, phi, Pr, Mr) at the single neutral-axis depth c_gov, strand by strand.

9. Resultant bending axis (strain compatibility at the demand angle)

The demand moment is resisted about the axis of the resultant moment. The interaction sweep is repeated with the section rotated by the folded angle alpha (0 to 45 degrees, the square being symmetric); the demand ray from the origin meets the phi-curve at (Pr, Mr) and D/C = Mu / Mr along the ray. The angle and that point are read from the sweep (amber inputs); tan(alpha) = M_min / M_max proves the angle, and the check at c_gov below recomputes the section.
